files.reduce_decisions.nl:
---
args: {}
returns: "Record<string, Decision>"
kind: directory-reducer
---
Read the task contract and every item in the directory. Read each item file for that item’s ID, state, question, and options. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. Compose the item question into the inline natural-language instruction at runtime. Pass case ID, state, question, options, levels separately. Do not combine fields into a serialized prompt variable or add captures for absent metadata. Save decisions.json and return that exact map.

files.reduce_decisions.nl:
---
args: {}
returns: "Record<string, Decision>"
kind: directory-reducer
---
Read the task contract and every item in the directory. Read each item file for that item’s ID, state, question, and options. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. Compose the item question into the inline natural-language instruction at runtime. Pass case ID, state, question, options, levels separately. Do not combine fields into a serialized prompt variable or add captures for absent metadata. Save decisions.json and return that exact map.

files.reduce_decisions.nl:
---
args: {}
returns: "Record<string, Decision>"
kind: directory-reducer
---
Read the task contract and every item in the directory. Read each item file for that item’s ID, state, question, and options. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. Compose the item question into the inline natural-language instruction at runtime. Pass case ID, state, question, options, levels separately. Do not combine fields into a serialized prompt variable or add captures for absent metadata. Save decisions.json and return that exact map.

files.reduce_decisions.nl:
---
args: {}
returns: "Record<string, Decision>"
kind: directory-reducer
---
Read the task contract and every item in the directory. Read each item file for that item’s ID, state, question, and options. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. Compose the item question into the inline natural-language instruction at runtime. Pass case ID, state, question, options, levels separately. Do not combine fields into a serialized prompt variable or add captures for absent metadata. Save decisions.json and return that exact map.

files.reduce_decisions.nl:
---
args: {}
returns: "Record<string, Decision>"
kind: directory-reducer
---
Read the task contract and every item in the directory. Read each item file for that item’s ID, state, question, and options. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. Compose the item question into the inline natural-language instruction at runtime. Pass case ID, state, question, options, levels separately. Do not combine fields into a serialized prompt variable or add captures for absent metadata. Save decisions.json and return that exact map.

files.reduce_decisions.nl:
---
args: {}
returns: "Record<string, Decision>"
kind: directory-reducer
---
Read the task contract and every item in the directory. Read each item file for that item’s ID, state, question, and options. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. Compose the item question into the inline natural-language instruction at runtime. Pass case ID, state, question, options, levels separately. Do not combine fields into a serialized prompt variable or add captures for absent metadata. Save decisions.json and return that exact map.

files.reduce_decisions.nl:
---
args: {}
returns: "Record<string, Decision>"
kind: directory-reducer
---
Read the task contract and every item in the directory. Read each item file for that item’s ID, state, question, and options. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. Compose the item question into the inline natural-language instruction at runtime. Pass case ID, state, question, options, levels separately. Do not combine fields into a serialized prompt variable or add captures for absent metadata. Save decisions.json and return that exact map.

files.reduce_decisions.nl:
---
args: {}
returns: "Record<string, Decision>"
kind: directory-reducer
---
Read the task contract and every item in the directory. Read each item file for that item’s ID, state, question, and options. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. Compose the item question into the inline natural-language instruction at runtime. Pass case ID, state, question, options, levels separately. Do not combine fields into a serialized prompt variable or add captures for absent metadata. Save decisions.json and return that exact map.

files.reduce_decisions.nl:
---
args: {}
returns: "Record<string, Decision>"
kind: directory-reducer
---
Read the task contract and every item in the directory. Read each item file for that item’s ID, state, question, and options. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. Compose the item question into the inline natural-language instruction at runtime. Pass case ID, state, question, options, levels separately. Do not combine fields into a serialized prompt variable or add captures for absent metadata. Save decisions.json and return that exact map.

files.reduce_decisions.nl:
---
args: {}
returns: "Record<string, Decision>"
kind: directory-reducer
---
Read the task contract and every item in the directory. Read each item file for that item’s ID, state, question, and options. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. Compose the item question into the inline natural-language instruction at runtime. Pass case ID, state, question, options, levels separately. Do not combine fields into a serialized prompt variable or add captures for absent metadata. Save decisions.json and return that exact map.

files.reduce_decisions.nl:
---
args: {}
returns: "Record<string, Decision>"
kind: directory-reducer
---
Read the task contract and every item in the directory. Read each item file for that item’s ID, state, question, and options. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. Compose the item question into the inline natural-language instruction at runtime. Pass case ID, state, question, options, levels separately. files.reduce_decisions.nl:
---
args: {}
returns: "Record<string, Decision>"
kind: directory-reducer
---
Read the task contract and every item in the directory. Read each item file for that item’s ID, state, question, and options. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. ---
Read the task contract and every item in the directory. Read each item file for that item’s ID, state, question, and options. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. Compose the item question into the inline natural-language instruction at runtime. Pass case ID, state, question, options, levels separately. files.reduce_decisions.nl:
---
args: {}
returns: "Record<string, Decision>"
kind: directory-reducer
---
Read the task contract and every item in the directory. Read each item file for that item’s ID, state, question, and options. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. Compose the item question into the inline natural-language instruction at runtime. Pass case ID, state, question, options, levels separately. Do not combine fields into a serialized prompt variable or add captures for absent metadata. Save decisions.json and return that exact map.

files.reduce_decisions.nl:
---
args: {}
returns: "Record<string, Decision>"
kind: directory-reducer
---
Read the task contract and every item in the directory. Read each item file for that item’s ID, state, question, and options. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. Compose the item question into the inline natural-language instruction at runtime. Pass case ID, state, question, options, levels separately. files.reduce_decisions.nl:
---
args: {}
returns: "Record<string, Decision>"
kind: directory-reducer
---
Read the task contract and every item in the directory. Read each item file for that item’s ID, state, question, and options. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. Compose the item question into the inline natural-language instruction at runtime. Pass case ID, state, question, options, levels separately. Do not combine fields into a serialized prompt variable or add captures for absent metadata. Save decisions.json and return that exact map.

Read the task contract and every item in the directory. Read each item file for that item’s ID, state, question, and options. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. Compose the item question into the inline natural-language instruction at runtime. Pass case ID, state, question, options, levels separately. Do not combine fields into a serialized prompt variable or add captures for absent metadata. Save decisions.json and return that exact map.

files.reduce_decisions.nl:
---
args: {}
returns: "Record<string, Decision>"
kind: directory-reducer
---
Read the task contract and every item in the directory. Read each item file for that item’s ID, state, question, and options. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. Compose the item question into the inline natural-language instruction at runtime. Pass case ID, state, question, options, levels separately. Do not combine fields into a serialized prompt variable or add captures for absent metadata. Save decisions.json and return that exact map.

Read the task contract and every item in the directory. Read each item file for that item’s ID, state, question, and options. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. Compose the item question into the inline natural-language instruction at runtime. Pass case ID, state, question, options, levels separately. Do not combine fields into a serialized prompt variable or add captures for absent metadata. Save decisions.json and return that exact map.

files.reduce_decisions.nl:
---
args: {}
returns: "Record<string, Decision>"
kind: directory-reducer
---
Read the task contract and every item in the directory. Read each item file for that item’s ID, state, question, and options. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. Compose the item question into the inline natural-language instruction at runtime. Pass case ID, state, question, options, levels separately. Do not combine fields into a serialized prompt variable or add captures for absent metadata. Save decisions.json and return that exact map.

minimum_sequence: read the runtime contract and directory items
capture case ID, state, question, options, levels from the item and task files
compose the item question into the typed inline instruction and follow the choice-specific output rule
pass all captures separately for every item
save and return the exact aggregate map

calls.code: console.log(JSON.stringify({ caseId, state, question, options, levels }));

files.reduce_decisions.nl:
---
args: {}
returns: "Record<string, Decision>"
kind: directory-reducer
---
Read the task contract and every item in the directory. Read each item file for that item’s ID, state, question, and options. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. ---
args: {}
returns: "Record<string, Decision>"
kind: directory-reducer
---
Read the task contract and every item in the directory. Read each item file for that item’s ID, state, question, and options. Preserve its options exactly; use task options only when that item has no options field. Use the supplied options without a separate rubric; only criteria read from an item or task file are authoritative. Levels are shared from task.json unless an item supplies its own levels; an explicit empty task levels list means no levels are supplied. Bind this item’s available fields before creating its inline natural-language function. Create that function inside the item’s callback so its question interpolation uses the bound question, and pass only supplied fields as separate arguments. Compose the item question into the inline natural-language instruction at runtime. Pass case ID, state, question, options, levels separately. Do not combine fields into a serialized prompt variable or add captures for absent metadata. Save decisions.json and return that exact map.
